reasons: No tests are visible for this file.
The login redirect runs inside a shared helper, so individual calls cannot opt out.
Data never going stale is a risky default, and the code gives no stated reason for it.

terms.meaning: A stored copy of server data kept in the browser so pages do not fetch it again each time.
A secret string that proves the user is logged in.
The server's reply meaning the request was not made by a logged-in user.
Old data that may no longer match the server.
Sending a failed request again automatically.

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports for the data client
sections.what: Brings in the data caching library and the function that supplies the login token.
sections.why: Likely reason: the shared data layer needs both to work.
sections.watch_out: The token comes from the login hook, so moving or renaming that hook breaks every request.

sections.name: authHeaders
sections.title: Attaching the login token to requests
sections.what: Builds the authorization header from the stored login token, or an empty header when the visitor is not logged in.
sections.why: Likely reason: the server checks this token on each request.
sections.watch_out: The token is read at the moment each request is made, so logging out takes effect on the next request.

sections.name: throwIfResNotOk
sections.title: Turning failed requests into errors
sections.what: Throws an error for any failed response. For a 401 it also sends the visitor to the login page unless they are already there. The error text includes the status code and the server message.
sections.why: Likely reason: a failed call should stop normal processing and let the page show a problem.
sections.watch_out: The redirect and the error both happen, so code that catches the error may still run while the page is leaving.

sections.name: apiRequest
sections.title: Sending a request that changes data
sections.what: Sends a request with a chosen method, such as POST or PUT, and an optional body. It adds the login token, throws on failure, and returns the response on success.
sections.why: Likely reason: one helper for create, update and delete calls, so each call does not repeat the header and error code.
sections.watch_out: A body that is zero or empty text is skipped and not sent, and the successful response body is left for the caller to read.

sections.name: UnauthorizedBehavior
sections.title: Fetching data for the cache
sections.what: Defines how the cache fetches data for a key: it joins the key parts into a web address, sends the token, and returns the parsed data. On a 401 it either returns nothing or throws, depending on the setting.
sections.why: Likely reason: some pages should show empty content when logged out, while others should show an error.
sections.watch_out: Key parts are joined with slashes to form the address, so a key part that already contains a slash or is an object builds a wrong address.

sections.name: queryClient
sections.title: Shared default settings for data fetching
sections.what: Creates the shared cache with its defaults: fetch from the address in the key, never refetch on a timer or when the window regains focus, treat data as fresh forever, and do not retry. Changes also do not retry.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code. The defaults look aimed at fewer server calls.
sections.watch_out: Data never goes stale, so a page can keep showing old numbers until it is reloaded or the cache is refreshed by hand.

summary: Sets up the shared data cache and the helper that sends requests with the login token.
purpose: Lets every page load and change data the same way, including login handling.
why: Likely reason: one place for default data behavior. The code gives few stated reasons for its defaults.
how: 1. Adds the login token to each request. 2. Turns failed responses into errors. 3. Sends the visitor to the login page on a 401 response. 4. Sets cache defaults: data is treated as fresh forever, no automatic refetch, no retries.
inputs: Requests from pages, the login token from the login hook, and server responses.
outputs: Parsed data for the cache, errors for failed calls, and redirects to the login page.
risks: Data never refreshes on its own, so old numbers can stay on screen. A 401 response redirects the page and can interrupt work. Failed requests are never retried, so a brief network drop shows an error.
debug: If a page shows old data, check whether it refreshes the cache after saving. If visitors are sent to login unexpectedly, check the login token and the 401 response. If a request fails, read the status and text in the error message.
